subject: Private upgrade: phased deploy & rollback roadmap
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, ops@acmecorp.com
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Private upgrade: phased deploy & rollback roadmap

Hi team,

Following our ops review, I put together a proposed phased rollout and rollback roadmap for the upcoming Private (VPC/on‑prem) maintenance window. Goal: ship the patch set with minimal customer impact and a clear, testable rollback path. High level:

• Phase A – Staging canary (10% of traffic) on Friday staging region, KV cache warmup, smoke tests (30m).
• Phase B – Narrow production canary (5% traffic) during quiet window, 1h observation and gating.
• Phase C – Progressive rollout: 25% → 50% → 100% with 30–60m observation at each step.

Key operational controls and requirements:
- Version pinning: customers on pinned versions will be left untouched unless they opt in; we will only update non‑pinned pools.
- Maintenance windows: prefer SAT 02:00–06:00 UTC (low token volume); if customers request different windows, we gate via the change request process.
- Network quiesce: drain connections for 60s prior to cutover per platform drain playbook.
- Rollback triggers: error rate >1.5% sustained for 5m OR token latency p95 regression >2× baseline for 10m.
- Rollback action: immediate rollback to prior pinned image + KV cache TTL reset; if rollback fails, initiate failover to backup region.

Attached: vpc-upgrade-phases.xlsx (phases + timeline), rollback-playbook.md (step checklist), patch-matrix.csv (models, quantization, compat notes).

Asks:
1) Naomi — can we tighten the canary gating metrics and add a KV retrofit test to the staging step?
2) Markus — confirm SLA gating thresholds are acceptable and advise if the rollback window needs extension.
3) ops@acmecorp.com / Mercantile — confirm you can support drain + kv reset in the SAT window or propose alternatives.

If everyone is aligned, I’ll file SUP-1423 and schedule the dry run.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, ops@acmecorp.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private upgrade: phased deploy & rollback roadmap

Thanks Karthik — good framework. A couple of practical tweaks from the staging/ops side:

• Canary gating: add an explicit SLI for token correctness (rerun canonical prompt set) and require 95% pass for canary success. Latency is necessary but not sufficient.
• KV cache warmup: we should include a scripted warmup that seeds top 500 prefixes. Expect ~12m for full seed; plan that into the 30m smoke window.
• Drain time: 60s may be tight for long‑lived connections in some on‑prem environments — recommend configurable drain up to 180s with a forced close after that.

I also attached a short checklist I maintain for staging dry runs — I’ll paste the main items into the runbook before the dry run.

On the maintenance window: Sat 02:00–06:00 UTC is generally fine for our EU/AP customers, but Mercantile has a weekend billing batch on Saturdays, so ops@acmecorp.com should confirm.

On rollback triggers: I agree with the 1.5% error threshold but propose we add a soft alert at 0.8% so engineers can intervene before automatic rollback.

Cheers,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

+1 to Naomi’s sanity checks. A few addenda from the SLA/ops governance side:

• SLA gating and rollback timing: automatic rollback is OK, but the SLA team needs a 30‑minute manual review window before a full fleet rollback for high‑impact tenants (top 10% by spend). That manual window should only apply if the soft alert threshold is hit; automatic rollback still applies for the hard trigger.
• Patch hold: for models marked 'high risk' in the patch-matrix.csv we require a signoff from Model Ops (so include Model Ops in the preflight checklist).
• Observability hooks: please ensure the canary includes tracing (trace ids preserved) and token‑level error tagging — that will speed triage.

If we keep the drain configurable (Naomi’s suggestion) and add the soft alert, I’m comfortable with the phased percentages and the rollback playbook as written.

Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

>
> 1) We can’t do the Sat 02:00–06:00 UTC window this time — we have a billing reconciliation batch that runs 03:00–05:00 UTC on Saturdays. Weekend maintenance must not overlap with that.
> 2) We require the KV cache rebuild test as Naomi described — we will run a simulated cold start to validate reconnection and cache seeding.
> 3) We prefer a Sunday early‑morning window: Sun 04:00–08:00 UTC. If Redwood can’t shift, we can provide a narrow 02:00–03:30 UTC window but require a rollback contact list with telephone numbers.
>
> We’ll coordinate with ops@acmecorp.com for the network‑drain windows and will confirm the exact start time by EOD tomorrow.
>

I’ll wait for final confirmation on window and the SUP-1423 ticket before we sign the dry‑run.

—Mercantile SRE
